name: Great Sand Dunes National Park and Preserve
blurb: Tallest dunes in North America, kangaroo rats and a beetle found nowhere else.

tip.title: Dry up the snowmelt
tip.text: Snowmelt feeds Medano Creek and the moist sand. Set Snowmelt and Medano Creek to -100% and watch the plants, then the seed and leaf eaters and their predators.

notes: The story and why it matters come from the Wikipedia articles listed below (Great Sand Dunes National Park and Preserve, Ord's kangaroo rat, Eriocoma hymenoides). Individual species and links have not been checked one by one. Feeding links that match a GloBI (Global Biotic Interactions) record are marked in the node details, with a link to the records. A few links were added from GloBI records.

nodes.desc: High-altitude sun powers the sparse plants of the dune field and the grasslands around it.
A small pine of the drier slopes, listed by Wikipedia among the park's trees. Its large seeds are a food for birds and rodents.
A hardy shrub of the sandy shrublands around the dunes that deer can browse.
A bunchgrass of sandy ground that Wikipedia says is eaten by elk, mule deer and others, and whose seeds feed many rodents and birds.
A common, widely recorded rodent that eats seeds and insects and is prey for snakes, hawks and coyotes.
Mostly eats seeds and caches them in burrows in loose sand. Coyotes, owls, hawks and snakes prey on it.
Browses shrubs and grazes grasses. Wikipedia says cougars hunt it at night in the montane woodlands.
Visits the dunes from surrounding habitats and grazes grasses such as ricegrass. Cougars take it, and coyotes and ravens use carcasses.
A large constrictor of the drier woodlands and sand country that eats rodents such as kangaroo rats and deer mice.
Wikipedia says raptors hunt mice and kangaroo rats over the sand sheet. Red-tailed hawks also take snakes.
The most recorded bird near the park. Eats insects and small animals and scavenges carcasses.
Wikipedia says cougars hunt mule deer at night in the park's montane woodlands. Elk are also a large prey.
Eats rodents, snakes, beetles and carcasses, and takes deer and elk. It hunts the sand sheet and woodlands.

story: Great Sand Dunes National Park in Colorado holds the tallest sand dunes in North America, up to 750 feet high, covering about 30 square miles. Winds from the southwest blew the sand against the Sangre de Cristo Mountains over tens of thousands of years. Visitors walk across the shallow Medano Creek in spring and summer to reach them.
matters: The system has four parts: the mountain watershed, the dune field, the sand sheet and the sabkha. Its watershed includes alpine tundra, subalpine forest and riparian zones.
